documents.title: Machine_4 Industrial Pump — Operating Manual
documents.content: Machine_4 is an Industrial Centrifugal Pump located in Zone B - Bay 2. Normal operating ranges: Temperature 45–70°C (fluid temperature, optimal 55–60°C), Vibration 0.06–0.18 mm/s, RPM 2800–3400 (optimal 3000), Power Consumption 850–1100 W. Pump type: Centrifugal, single stage. Flow rate: 50 m³/hr at 3000 RPM. Head: 30 meters. Motor rating: 1.1 kW. Fluid handled: Water/coolant mixture, max viscosity 50 cSt. Maximum fluid temperature: 80°C. Suction pressure: Minimum 0.5 bar. Discharge pressure: Maximum 5 bar. Impeller diameter: 150 mm. Shaft seal type: Mechanical seal. Startup procedure: (1) Ensure suction valve is fully open, (2) Close discharge valve partially, (3) Prime pump — ensure pump casing is full of fluid, (4) Start motor, (5) Slowly open discharge valve to operating position, (6) Verify flow and pressure are within normal range. Shutdown procedure: (1) Close discharge valve slowly, (2) Stop motor, (3) Close suction valve if maintenance required, (4) Drain pump if ambient temperature below 0°C.

documents.title: Machine_4 Industrial Pump — Maintenance Schedule
documents.content: Machine_4 Industrial Pump Preventive Maintenance Schedule. DAILY: Check mechanical seal for leakage — acceptable leakage is 1-3 drops per minute. Check bearing housing temperature by touch — should not be hot to touch. Listen for cavitation noise (grinding or rattling sound). Monitor suction pressure gauge — must remain above 0.5 bar. Check pump and motor for unusual vibration. WEEKLY: Lubricate bearing housing with correct grease — 5g per bearing. Check coupling alignment visually. Inspect suction strainer and clean if blocked. Check all bolts and mounting for tightness. Test balance of flow by checking inlet and outlet pressures. MONTHLY: Full bearing inspection — check for play or noise. Mechanical seal replacement if leakage exceeds 5 drops per minute. Check impeller wear by measuring flow rate against baseline. Inspect motor windings resistance. Clean pump casing exterior. Check and calibrate all pressure gauges. EVERY 2000 HOURS: Replace mechanical seal regardless of condition. Inspect impeller for wear, cavitation damage or corrosion. Check wear rings clearance — replace if clearance exceeds 0.5mm. Replace bearing grease completely. ANNUALLY: Full pump overhaul — disassemble, inspect all internal parts, replace wear rings, mechanical seal, bearings. Motor insulation test. Verify pump curve against original specification.

documents.title: Machine_4 Industrial Pump — Alert Explanations
documents.content: Machine_4 Industrial Pump Alert Guide. CAVITATION ALERT — Most Critical Issue (RPM drop + HIGH VIBRATION simultaneously): Cavitation is the most damaging condition for centrifugal pumps. Causes: suction pressure too low (below 0.5 bar), suction valve partially closed, high fluid temperature (reduces NPSH), blocked suction strainer, pump running at too high flow rate. Symptoms: Grinding or rattling noise, increased vibration, erratic flow, reduced pressure. Actions: IMMEDIATELY reduce flow rate by closing discharge valve 20%, check suction strainer, verify suction pressure is above 0.5 bar. Prolonged cavitation will destroy impeller within hours. HIGH VIBRATION ALERT (Warning >0.3 mm/s, Critical >0.5 mm/s): Causes include cavitation (see above), worn bearings, bent shaft, impeller damage, pump running off best efficiency point, coupling misalignment. Actions: Check for cavitation symptoms first. If no cavitation, schedule bearing inspection within 4 hours. MECHANICAL SEAL FAILURE (fluid leak): Causes include dry running (never run pump without fluid), abrasive particles in fluid, excessive temperature, shaft misalignment. Actions: Stop pump if leakage is continuous stream — risk of electrical fault from water reaching motor. Replace seal before restart. HIGH TEMPERATURE ALERT (Warning >70°C, Critical >80°C): Causes include insufficient flow through pump (pump running against closed valve), bearing failure, high ambient temperature, thick fluid. Actions: Verify discharge valve is open, check cooling water flow. POWER SPIKE ALERT (Warning >1300 W): Indicates bearing seizure, impeller jammed, foreign object in pump. Actions: Emergency stop immediately.

documents.title: Machine_4 Industrial Pump — Operator Guidelines
documents.content: Machine_4 Industrial Pump Operator Guidelines. SAFETY RULES: Never start pump with suction valve closed — causes immediate seal and bearing damage. Never run pump dry even for a few seconds — destroys mechanical seal. Always relieve pressure before any maintenance work — open drain valve to confirm zero pressure. Wear face shield when opening any pump connections — fluid may be under pressure. Report any continuous fluid leak immediately — do not leave unattended. OPERATING TIPS: Always prime pump before starting — pump must be full of fluid. Start pump with discharge valve at 30% open, then gradually open fully. Monitor vibration level — increase indicates developing fault. If pump loses prime, stop immediately and re-prime before restart. For best efficiency, operate pump at 2800-3200 RPM range. LOSS OF PRIME PROCEDURE: Stop motor immediately. Close discharge valve. Open priming plug and add fluid until full. Close priming plug securely. Restart following normal startup procedure. If pump loses prime repeatedly, check suction piping for air leaks. CAVITATION RECOGNITION: Noisy rattling or grinding sound from pump casing, fluctuating flow and pressure readings, increased vibration, reduced efficiency. If cavitation suspected, reduce flow immediately and investigate suction conditions. SHIFT HANDOVER CHECKLIST: Record mechanical seal leakage rate (drops per minute), note bearing temperature, record any unusual noise, log suction and discharge pressures, record any cavitation events during shift, check gland packing or seal condition.
